guide_enrichment.narrative:
We see the clearest separation risk in Texas’ passing game against a UT San Antonio defense that grades poorly against the pass. That concern extends beyond one strong opener: Manning produced 3,163 passing yards and 26 touchdowns across 13 starts last season, and Texas returns four starters on the offensive line. The continuity around the quarterback helps explain why our numbers give Texas a substantial offensive advantage here.

The counter is UT San Antonio’s passing offense against a Texas pass defense that has not graded at the same level as the Longhorns’ offense. That gives UT San Antonio a plausible path to scoring enough to remain competitive against a large margin. We also account for the turnover risk after Texas forced three in its opener, but we are not treating one game as proof that those extra possessions will repeat. For us, the competing passing-game signals leave our expectation essentially in line with the market, so the current price does not create enough value.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch:
We are watching Manning and the Texas receivers against UT San Antonio’s pass defense. Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the opener, while Ryan Wingo had 121 receiving yards and Cam Coleman added 70 yards with two scores. We care less about the final margin from that game than the variety of proven receiving options Texas showed.

If UT San Antonio can limit explosive completions and force Texas to sustain drives, we see a better chance for the underdog to stay within range. If not, this is the matchup most likely to create separation.

recent_game.fact: Texas opened the 2026 season with a 59-7 home win over Texas State on Sept. 5.
Texas produced 516 total yards and averaged 7.0 yards per play against Texas State.
Texas' running backs accounted for 156 rushing yards and three touchdowns against Texas State.
Texas forced three turnovers, consisting of two fumble recoveries and one interception, against Texas State.

opponent_notes.fact: The 2026 game will be the third meeting between Texas and UTSA, and all three meetings have been scheduled in Austin.

quarterback.fact: Senior quarterback Arch Manning completed 20 of 27 passes for 305 yards and four touchdowns in the 2026 opener against Texas State.
Manning is 13-3 as a Texas starter, including 9-0 at DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium.
In 13 starts during 2025, Manning completed 248 of 404 passes for 3,163 yards and 26 touchdowns and added 399 rushing yards and a team-high 10 rushing touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers transferred to Texas in spring 2026 from Arizona State and NC State, respectively.
Smothers recorded 72 rushing yards on 10 attempts and caught three passes for 28 yards and a touchdown against Texas State.
Brown recorded 34 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 11 carries in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Ryan Wingo caught seven passes for 121 yards and one touchdown in the season opener.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman caught three passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his Texas debut against Texas State.
Texas added tight end Michael Masunas from Michigan State; he played in the opener after recording 19 catches for 232 yards and three touchdowns in 2025.
Four 2025 offensive-line starters return in 2026: Trevor Goosby, Brandon Baker, Cole Hutson and Connor Robertson.
Texas added offensive linemen Laurence Seymore III, Melvin Siani and Dylan Sikorski through the transfer portal; the listed offensive-line group entered 2026 with 226 combined games and 114 starts.

defensive_personnel.fact: Senior defensive back Jelani McDonald led Texas with eight tackles, including seven solo tackles and one tackle for loss, in the season opener.
EDGE Colin Simmons recorded one tackle, a half tackle for loss, one quarterback hurry and a fumble recovery against Texas State.
Simmons led Texas in 2025 with 15.5 tackles for loss, 12 sacks, 15 pressures, three forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.
Texas added defensive transfers Rasheem Biles, Markus Boswell, Justin Cryer, Darius Snow, Ian Geffrard, Zion Williams, Nick Hudson and Bo Mascoe for 2026.

coaching_changes.fact: Texas' 2026 staff lists Kyle Flood as offensive coordinator and offensive-line coach and AJ Milwee as co-offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach.
Texas' 2026 staff lists Will Muschamp as defensive coordinator and Johnny Nansen as co-defensive coordinator and linebackers coach.

offensive_context.fact: Texas scored on 100 percent of its red-zone opportunities and converted 45.5 percent of its third downs in the season opener.
Texas did not punt against Texas State, its first game without a punt since playing Kansas in 2023.

defensive_context.fact: Texas allowed 165 total yards, including 45 rushing yards and 120 passing yards, in the season opener.
Texas has forced a turnover in 24 consecutive home games and in 36 of its last 37 games.
Texas has recorded 57 takeaways since the start of the 2024 season.

special_teams.fact: Texas added punter Mac Chiumento from Florida State, kicker Gianni Spetic from Memphis and deep snapper Trey Dubuc from New Mexico for 2026.
